25 ♠ GTO CRASH COURSE - STRATEGY GUIDE


    VIDEO 5


  Exploitation (A-5 Game)
  Explotation in the
  A-5 Game - In the              Coach:
  previous lesson, you           Andrew Brokos
  learned how to apply
  equilibrium strategy           Video Length:
  to the A-5 game.               25:33
  In this lesson we
  look at exploitation
  strategies, specifically with regards to over-folding,
  under-bluffing and nitty checking.

  Profitable opportunities to exploit when our opponent
  folds too much, bluffs too infrequently, or checks too
  much – these are common mistakes among the poker
  population. Learning the theory behind how to exploit
  these mistakes allows you to know why exploitation
  works.

  Additionally in this video, you are greeted with numerous
  opportunities to predict the probable actions of the
  different players. How will the OOP player respond to
  mistakes by the IP player? Will he bluff more, value bet
  more, with what? We encourage you to take the time while
  watching the video to make predictions, and then use the
  quiz questions to see if you integrated what you learned.

## PDF page 29

```text
29 ♠ GTO CRASH COURSE - STRATEGY GUIDE


                  Nitty-Checking Question:

  4. What if IP always checks a Ten? How would OOP’s
  strategy change? Remember that IP at optimal levels
  will sometimes bet when holding a Ten.



         In the IP nitty-checking scenario, OOP
         always bets Aces to Jacks and bluffs with
         a mixed strategy with Sixes and Fives.
         Since IP will not thin value bet enough, the
         optimal response is to never check value
         bets. The reasonSHOW   ANSWER
                            behind  this is that without
         a thin value betting strategy, IP makes it
         less profitable for OOP to check with value
         hands, because they will never catch a thin
         value bet.
```
